english.title: Misuse profits of exempt lottery - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used part of the profits of

(A)_[an incidental non-commercial lottery within the meaning of Part 1]_
(B)_[a private society lottery within the meaning of Part 2]_
(C)_[a small society lottery within the meaning of Part 4]_

of Schedule 11 to the Gambling Act 2005 for a purpose other than one for which the lottery was permitted to be promoted in accordance with Schedule 11
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 261 and 263(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Sections 261(3) and 260(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provide that "using profits" includes permitting profits to be used.
(ii) For the territorial application of this offence see section 265 of the Gambling Act 2005.
(iii) A licensing authority may institute criminal proceedings in respect of this offence, section 346(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
